about.heading: About My Focus
about.body:
As a Renewable Energy Engineer with a background in Engineering Physics from Universitas Gadjah Mada, my work sits at the intersection of technical rigor and sustainable vision. I specialize in New and Renewable Energy (EBT), Building Physics, and Acoustics, focusing on comprehensive planning, system modeling, and data-driven execution.

My research is deeply rooted in utilizing advanced modeling tools to forecast energy needs and optimize transitions. I believe that effective sustainability requires not just idealism, but precise, technical recommendations grounded in robust GIS analysis and simulation.

works.title: Agrovoltaic Smart Farming System
works.short_desc: Supported the field implementation of an agrovoltaic system combining solar PV technology with agriculture.
works.description:
Role: Research Staff

Organization: Renewable Energy Systems, Applications, and Planning (RESP)

Duration: 2026 – Present

Focus: Solar PV Installation, Agrovoltaics, Sustainable Agriculture

Tools: Solar PV Systems, Electrical Wiring & Installation, Power Tools, Structural Installation, Field Engineering Practices

Problem:

Agricultural operations in rural communities often face increasing energy costs and limited access to sustainable energy solutions. At the same time, farmers need to maintain productivity while adapting to climate change and improving resource efficiency. Integrating solar energy generation with agricultural activities presents an opportunity to address both challenges simultaneously.

Action:

Supported the field implementation of an agrovoltaic system that combines solar photovoltaic (PV) technology with agricultural land use. Assisted in the installation of PV support structures, cable routing, equipment assembly, and site preparation activities. Collaborated with researchers, engineers, and local stakeholders during the deployment of renewable energy infrastructure for smart farming applications.

Outcome:

Successfully contributed to the construction and deployment phase of the agrovoltaic system by supporting on-site installation activities and infrastructure preparation. The project established the foundation for integrating renewable energy technologies into community-based agricultural operations.

Key Learnings:

- Solar photovoltaic (PV) installation practices.

- Renewable energy system deployment.

- Field engineering and construction workflows.

- Electrical installation and equipment assembly.

- Collaboration within multidisciplinary research teams.

- Community-based renewable energy implementation.

works.title: Undergraduate Thesis Research
works.short_desc: Spatial Analysis of Renewable Energy Mix Potential in Kulon Progo Regency with the 2060 Energy Transition Scenario
works.description:
Role: Undergraduate Thesis Researcher

Duration: 2026 – Present

Focus: Renewable Energy Assessment, GIS, Energy System Modeling, Sustainability Planning

Tools: QGIS, NREL System Advisor Model (SAM), LEAP, Analytic Network Process (ANP), Remote Sensing & Spatial Analysis, Data Processing & Visualization

Problem:

Achieving Indonesia's 2060 energy transition target requires region-specific renewable energy planning based on accurate resource assessments and long-term energy demand projections. However, the renewable energy potential of Kulon Progo Regency has not been comprehensively evaluated through an integrated framework that combines spatial suitability analysis, energy generation modeling, and energy transition scenarios.

Action:

Conducting a comprehensive assessment of renewable energy resources in Kulon Progo Regency through the integration of GIS-based spatial analysis, renewable energy simulation, and energy system modeling. The study evaluates the technical potential of solar, wind, hydropower, and biomass resources while considering geographical, environmental, infrastructure, and land-use constraints.

Renewable energy generation potential is simulated using the NREL System Advisor Model (SAM), while future energy transition pathways are analyzed using the Long-range Energy Alternatives Planning System (LEAP). The Analytic Network Process (ANP) is applied to prioritize renewable energy technologies and determine the most suitable energy mix under the 2060 transition scenario.

Outcome:

Developing a data-driven renewable energy transition roadmap that identifies suitable development zones, estimates renewable energy generation potential, and provides strategic recommendations for achieving a sustainable and resilient regional energy mix in Kulon Progo Regency.

Key Learnings:

- Renewable Energy Resource Assessment
- GIS-Based Spatial Suitability Analysis
- Energy Generation Simulation
- Long-Term Energy System Modeling
- Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (ANP)
- Sustainable Energy Planning
- Environmental and Land-Use Assessment

works.title: KKN-PPM UGM Period II 2025 — Engineering & Community Development
works.short_desc: Led and implemented multiple community-based engineering projects in Cigugur, Kuningan, including energy-efficient lighting systems, IoT-powered smart irrigation, biopore infiltration systems, landslide early warning mechanisms, and educational space revitalization. Combined engineering solutions with community training to promote sustainable technology adoption and long-term local impact.
works.description:
Role: Village level student coordinator

Organization: Universitas Gadjah Mada

Location: Cigugur District

Duration: 2025

Focus: IoT, Renewable Energy, Appropriate Technology, Disaster Mitigation, Community Empowerment

Tools: ESP8266, IoT, Environmental Monitoring, Sustainable Energy, Disaster Mitigation, Community Development, Electrical Systems

Problem:

Rural communities often face challenges related to energy efficiency, agricultural productivity, environmental sustainability, disaster preparedness, and access to educational facilities. Many existing solutions remain manual, resource-intensive, and difficult to maintain over the long term.

Action:

Designed and implemented a series of community-based engineering projects that combined appropriate technology, environmental awareness, and local capacity building. The programs emphasized practical implementation, technology transfer, and sustainability through community participation and hands-on training.

Outcome:

Successfully delivered multiple technology and community development initiatives that promoted energy efficiency, environmental sustainability, smart agriculture, disaster preparedness, and educational accessibility. The projects were accompanied by training and knowledge transfer activities to support long-term adoption by local residents.

Key Learnings:

- Community-centered engineering design.
- IoT implementation in rural environments.
- Sustainable technology deployment.
- Project management and stakeholder engagement.
- Translating technical solutions into real-world impact.

---

### Featured Projects

**1. Automatic Light Control System Based on Light Sensors**

*Focus: Energy Efficiency & Sustainable Energy*

Designed and installed an automatic lighting system utilizing LDR-based light sensors and energy-efficient LED lamps. The system automatically adjusts lighting operation according to ambient light conditions, reducing unnecessary electricity consumption while promoting awareness of sustainable energy practices.

*Technologies: LDR Sensor, LED Lighting, Electrical Installation*

**2. Biopore Infiltration Holes for Organic Waste Management and Flood Mitigation**

*Focus: Environmental Sustainability*

Implemented biopore infiltration systems to improve rainwater absorption, reduce surface runoff, and support organic waste decomposition. Conducted community training sessions to ensure residents could independently construct and maintain the installations.

*Technologies: Biopore System, Environmental Engineering, Waste Management*

**3. Smart Irrigation and Environmental Monitoring System**

*Focus: IoT & Smart Agriculture*

Developed an automated irrigation system equipped with soil moisture, temperature, and humidity monitoring capabilities. The system utilized ESP8266 microcontrollers, sensors, and automated water pumps to optimize irrigation practices for local farmers and livestock owners.

*Technologies: ESP8266, IoT, Soil Moisture Sensors, Environmental Monitoring, Automation*

**4. Community Reading Corner Revitalization**

*Focus: Education & Community Development*

Designed and improved a community reading corner through spatial organization, educational visual materials, and environmental enhancements to create a more engaging learning environment for local residents and children.

*Technologies: Visual Design, Educational Media, Community Engagement*

**5. Landslide Early Warning and Ground Movement Monitoring System**

*Focus: Disaster Risk Reduction*

Developed a simple community-based early warning system for detecting potential ground movement and landslide risks. The project aimed to improve disaster preparedness and raise awareness regarding environmental hazards in vulnerable areas.

*Technologies: Early Warning Systems, Disaster Mitigation, Community Safety*

works.title: Ferrumium - PKM-K Funded Project (2023)
works.short_desc: Contributed to the design and development of Ferrumium, an upcycled product from used lighter components.
works.description:
Role: Product Design Staff

Duration: 2023

Tools: Blender 3D, AutoCAD 3D, Autodesk 3ds Max, Figma

Problem:

Thousands of used cigarette lighters are discarded every day despite containing reusable components and distinctive mechanical forms. The challenge was to transform this waste into a product that was both environmentally meaningful and commercially attractive.

Approach / Process:

Contributed to the design and development of Ferrumium, a collection of miniature robot figures created from recycled lighter components. Developed product concepts, explored design variations, and assisted in transforming raw materials into visually appealing collectibles. Worked closely with the team to balance aesthetics, manufacturability, and material constraints while maintaining the project's sustainability objectives.

Outcome:

Contributed to the successful development of an innovative upcycling product that secured funding through the PKM-K entrepreneurship program. The project demonstrated how discarded materials could be transformed into value-added products with creative and commercial potential.

Key Learnings:

- Sustainable product design and upcycling principles.

- Designing under material and manufacturing constraints.

- Converting conceptual ideas into tangible products.

- Cross-functional collaboration in an entrepreneurship project.

works.title: Society of Renewable Energy (SRE) UGM — Research & Innovation Division
works.short_desc: Contributed to renewable energy and sustainability initiatives through interdisciplinary research and engineering projects.

Role: Research & Innovation Member

Organization: Society of Renewable Energy (SRE) UGM

Tools: Solar PV, ESP32, IoT Systems, Photobioreactor Design, Blender, Figma, Technical Documentation

Contributed to renewable energy and sustainability initiatives through interdisciplinary research and engineering projects focused on bioenergy, solar energy integration, IoT-based agriculture systems, and community-centered technology implementation.

Problem:

Many renewable energy and sustainable agriculture solutions remain difficult to implement due to technical complexity, limited accessibility, and the lack of integrated systems that connect research concepts with real-world applications.

Approach / Process:

Collaborated within the Research & Innovation Division to develop renewable energy and smart agriculture projects. Contributed to the design of a photobioreactor prototype for microalgae-based biodiesel research, while also participating in the engineering design of a photovoltaic-powered smart drip irrigation system integrating solar energy, IoT monitoring, and automated irrigation control for sustainable farming applications.

Outcome:

Produced technical designs, system architectures, and engineering concepts that supported both research and community-oriented sustainability initiatives. The photobioreactor project was further developed and presented in a national scientific paper competition, while the smart irrigation project provided a practical framework for renewable-energy-powered agricultural technology deployment.

Key Learnings:

- Renewable Energy Systems
- Bioenergy Technologies
- Solar PV Applications
- Smart Agriculture
- IoT System Design
- Engineering Prototyping
- Technical Documentation
- Interdisciplinary Research

Impact Statement:

Designed and developed renewable energy and smart agriculture solutions by combining bioenergy research, solar PV integration, and IoT-based automation to support sustainable technology adoption.

works.title: Scientific Paper Competition EXPO 2024
works.short_desc: 3rd Place Winner - Designed a photobioreactor prototype for microalgae cultivation.
works.description:
Role: Photobioreactor Prototype Designer

Duration: 2024

Tools: Blender 3D, AutoCAD 3D, Autodesk 3ds Max, Figma

Award: 3rd Place Winner

Organizer: Universitas Lampung

Problem:

Despite the growing interest in microalgae-based biodiesel as a sustainable energy source, achieving economically viable production remains a significant challenge. Improvements in both biological engineering and cultivation systems are required to enhance biomass and lipid productivity.

Approach / Process:

Collaborated in the development of the research project "Bioengineering of Microalgae: Genome Editing of Chlamydomonas reinhardtii for Enhanced Biodiesel Productivity Through CRISPRi." Contributed by designing a photobioreactor prototype intended to support controlled microalgae cultivation and future implementation of genome-editing strategies. Developed conceptual designs, system visualizations, and engineering representations to communicate the integration of biotechnology and renewable energy applications.

Outcome:

The project was awarded 3rd Place at the Scientific Paper Competition EXPO 2024, recognizing its innovative approach to combining synthetic biology and sustainable energy technologies for future biodiesel production.

Key Learnings:

- Biofuel and renewable energy technologies.

- Photobioreactor engineering concepts.

- Scientific research communication.

- Translating research concepts into engineering prototypes.

- Interdisciplinary collaboration between biotechnology and engineering fields.

works.title: Photovoltaic-Powered Smart Drip Irrigation System for Bhumee Organic
works.short_desc: Designed a solar-powered smart drip irrigation system integrating IoT and automated control.
works.description:
Role: Research & Innovation Member

Organization: Society of Renewable Energy (SRE) UGM

Duration: 2024

Focus: Solar Energy Integration, IoT Systems, Smart Agriculture

Tools: Solar Energy Integration, IoT Systems, Smart Agriculture

Problem:

Bhumee Organic, an organic farming cooperative in Yogyakarta, relied on conventional irrigation methods that resulted in excessive water consumption, inefficient labor utilization, and difficulties in maintaining optimal soil moisture levels for dragon fruit cultivation.

Approach / Process:

Collaborated with a multidisciplinary team to design a photovoltaic-powered smart drip irrigation system for a 500 m² agricultural area. Contributed to the electrical system design and IoT architecture, including soil moisture monitoring, automated irrigation control, water level management, and remote system monitoring. The system integrated solar panels, energy storage, ESP32-based controllers, soil moisture sensors, pumps, and cloud-based monitoring to support precision agriculture practices.

Outcome:

Developed a sustainable irrigation solution capable of optimizing water usage, reducing manual labor requirements, and supporting data-driven irrigation management. The project demonstrated how renewable energy and IoT technologies can be integrated to improve agricultural efficiency and sustainability in small-scale farming operations.

Key Learnings:

- Solar-powered system design and integration.

- IoT architecture for agricultural automation.

- Sensor-based monitoring and control systems.

- Sustainable engineering for real-world community applications.

- Cross-disciplinary collaboration between engineering and agriculture.
